southIndianStatus.productLedExplanation: Seedai is exclusively Tamil Nadu — a small, round, fried snack made specifically for Krishna Jayanthi. There is no equivalent in any other Indian culinary tradition.
southIndianStatus.flavorLedExplanation: The butter-sesame-asafoetida flavor combination is distinctly South Indian. The specific ritual of making both sweet (vella) and savory (kara) seedai for Krishna Jayanthi makes this a culturally locked product.
southIndianStatus.overallSummary: Seedai is one of those rare products that is 100% product-led, 100% flavor-led, and 100% occasion-specific — it belongs to one state, one festival, and has no proxy elsewhere.

stateSpeciality.origin: Seedai is the primary offering for Krishna Jayanthi (Gokulashtami) in Tamil Nadu — the festival celebrating Lord Krishna's birth. The round shape represents Krishna's famous butter balls. Both kara seedai (savory) and vella seedai (sweet) are prepared.
stateSpeciality.culturalSignificance: Krishna Jayanthi in Tamil Nadu is incomplete without the triple preparation: murukku, kozhukattai, and seedai. Seedai is the one most associated with the festival's visual identity — the small round balls placed in front of Krishna's idol.
stateSpeciality.storytelling: The warning every Tamil grandmother gives before making seedai: if you rush the dough, the oil will remember. Seedai that isn't rolled tight enough will burst in the oil — not a soft pop, but an actual spray that clears the kitchen. Good seedai comes from dough rolled between both palms, patient and even, until it's perfectly spherical. The reward: a crisp, butter-fragrant ball that shatters cleanly when bitten.
stateSpeciality.bestSeason: Krishna Jayanthi (August) is the only season. Outside this window, demand drops sharply.

productDescriptors.title: The One That Bursts in the Oil
productDescriptors.descriptor: Every Tamil family has a seedai story — the year it exploded in the kadai and cleared the kitchen, the year it came out flat because the dough was too wet. Good seedai is rolled tight, uniform, patient. It doesn't burst. It slides into the oil and comes out perfectly spherical, crisp all the way through. Getting this right is a skill. These were made by someone who has been making them correctly for twenty years.
productDescriptors.rationale: Acknowledging the 'burst in the oil' failure mode before claiming mastery over it is the Pratfall Effect in action — admitting the risk builds credibility for the claim of getting it right.

productDescriptors.title: August's Smell, Bottled
productDescriptors.descriptor: The smell of seedai frying in the morning is August in Tamil Nadu. It means today is Krishna Jayanthi. It means the murukku press and the kozhukattai steamer are also going. It means the house will smell of sesame and butter and festival for the rest of the day. This box is not a snack. It is the specific smell of a specific morning, put somewhere you can open it later.
productDescriptors.principle: LOSS AVERSION + GEOGRAPHICAL PROVENANCE (Sutherland S3 + S5)
productDescriptors.rationale: The 'August smell' is a vivid, specific sensory anchor that makes non-ownership feel like a loss — exactly how loss aversion and geographical memory combine to create purchase urgency.
